identity.name: ADVIT JEWELS LIMITED
identity.industry: Consumer Discretionary — Luxury Handcrafted Bridal Jewellery (Kundan / Polki / Jadau)

summary.oneLiner: Jaipur-based manufacturer and seller of traditional and contemporary handcrafted fine jewellery (Kundan, Polki, Diamond and Studded) under the brand 'Rambhajo since 1921', operating largely on a B2B model.
summary.business: Advit Jewels manufactures 100% handmade fine jewellery - primarily Gold Kundan Meena Polki Jadau and cut-set diamond-with-Polki pieces (necklaces, earrings, rings, bangles and customized pieces) in 14- and 18-carat gold - from a single leased 6,450 sq ft unit in Jaipur that runs the full production cycle in-house. It sells predominantly B2B to dealers, showrooms and jewellery retailers, with a smaller B2C made-to-order business, and is setting up a flagship store in Jaipur. The 'Rambhajo' brand traces to a jewellery business established in 1921.

endMarkets: B2B - dealers, showrooms and jewellery retailers (82.41% of revenue in 9M FY26)|B2C - exclusive made-to-order pieces (17.39% in 9M FY26)|Job work (0.20% in 9M FY26)

currentContext.business: Advit Jewels manufactures 100% handmade fine jewellery - primarily Gold Kundan Meena Polki Jadau and cut-set diamond-with-Polki pieces (necklaces, earrings, rings, bangles and customized pieces) in 14- and 18-carat gold - from a single leased 6,450 sq ft unit in Jaipur that runs the full production cycle in-house. It sells predominantly B2B to dealers, showrooms and jewellery retailers, with a smaller B2C made-to-order business, and is setting up a flagship store in Jaipur. The 'Rambhajo' brand traces to a jewellery business established in 1921.
currentContext.expansion: The company is constructing a flagship retail store in Jaipur to grow its B2C business; manufacturing remains at the single leased 6,450 sq ft Jaipur unit (FY25 utilisation ~46%, leaving headroom).

one-line thesis: FY26 was the company's strongest year and its listing year — total income up 33.7% to INR 167.03 cr with PAT up 35.6% and a 29.5% EBITDA margin — but Q4 was materially softer (INR 43.23 cr against ~INR 60 cr a year earlier), which management attributes to war-driven caution in the luxury segment between January and March plus order timing pulled into the December quarter. The forward story is a B2B-to-B2C pivot: a franchise partner has committed 30 stores over three years, a ~30,000 sq ft Jaipur flagship is being fitted out, and management is deliberately capping FY27 at a minimum of three stores to learn first.
financial scorecard (track qoq/yoy):
| Metric | Q4 FY26 | FY26 (full year) | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| Total income | INR 43.23 cr | INR 167.03 cr, +33.68% | Q4 softer YoY — a shareholder cited ~INR 60 cr in the base quarter |
| EBITDA / margin | INR 12.56 cr / 29.04% | INR 49.24 cr / 29.48%, +32.52% | Margin essentially held despite the softer quarter |
| PAT | INR 8.74 cr | INR 34.39 cr, +35.56% | — |
| Diluted EPS | INR 2.79 | INR 10.74 | — |
| Order book | not disclosed | — | Company works to order; August order intake flagged as the next cycle |
| Cash / net debt | not disclosed on call | — | Listed on NSE and BSE during FY26 |
> Operating metrics: active customer base rose from 96 to 274; presence across 21 states; exports initiated but under 1% of FY26 revenue. Reported capacity utilisation of ~31% is measured on **gold weight only** and management argues it is not a meaningful metric for design-led Polki jewellery where stones, Polki and labour carry most of the value: "the statistics of weight don't work with the Advit Jewels jewellery actually." The disclosed product count fell from 21 to 10 purely because of recategorisation — five-piece bridal items are now counted as one bridal set, and hand-wear categories were consolidated.
guidance (critical — verify next quarter:
- **Revenue growth / EBITDA:** **no numeric FY27 guidance given.** Asked directly for revenue and EBITDA targets, management deferred to figures already disclosed in the DRHP and to the five-year projections on the company website, and could not restate them on the call — "I will have to check that because that was a number which was calculated that time."
- **Store rollout:** franchise partner Francorp "has committed to us to bring up 30 stores in next three years." Company's own FY27 plan is deliberately smaller: "we are setting up at least around three stores in this year. The target is minimum three… others are bonus for this year."
- **Flagship commissioning:** the ~30,000 sq ft Jaipur store is targeted for operations "by say November end, when the NRIs start coming, the wedding season starts coming" — explicitly not by Diwali.
- **Margin:** no target, but management stated pricing is on fixed margins irrespective of product mix — "we are just keeping the fixed margins. Whatever the cost comes, we just keep the margins fixed on."
- **Exports:** no timeline or number. Middle East trade shows being planned; UK flagged as an opportunity after the 15 July free-trade opening.
order book & pipeline: No order book disclosure. The business is seasonal and order-driven: management noted the September–December quarter is strong ("you will see an amazing increase in the sales") and that FY26 Q4 was partly cannibalised because orders received in December were completed and booked within that quarter. The next intake cycle was flagged for August, with artisans "all set to work hard." Post-IPO roadshows have produced an unexpected B2C funnel — management cited a Delhi roadshow attendee who subsequently bought five necklaces.
segment / subsidiary detail: Single-line business — 100% Jadau/Polki. Management rejects Titan and Kalyan as peers on the grounds that they are generic gold and diamond jewellers who "keep very little part of Jadau Polki. We are 100% Jadau Polki." The revenue split has moved toward B2C: "you can see it started touching 80 and 20." Gold content varies by piece rather than by rule — management gave the range explicitly: a new collection at ~30% gold value, men's buckles at ~70–80% gold value, and light earrings at very low gold content with Polki and coloured stone dominant. Exports were incidental in FY26 — an Instagram-originated US order where the customer absorbed a 50% tariff.
growth verticals / optionality:
- **Retail/B2C rollout:** the core optionality. 30 franchise stores committed over three years, three self-driven stores in FY27, plus LOIs in progress on additional locations.
- **Men's jewellery:** cufflinks, belt buckles, brooches, kilangi and rings in Polki — a new category with higher gold content.
- **Gen-Z lightweight line:** everyday-wear pieces at fixed margins.
- **Cross-regional design fusion:** blending Rajasthani Jadau with South Indian temple jewellery to widen geographic appeal — a named product initiative for the coming collection.
- **Exports:** UK (post-FTA), Middle East shows, and the Indian diaspora. Management is candid that nothing is built yet — "we are not yet started on that part yet."
6a. moat & competitive position:
- **Four-generation craft knowledge as an operating input, not marketing:** "I myself can make a Jadau by my hand." Management detailed genuinely operational know-how — that a karigar should not work a piece in humid or wet conditions, and that pieces made "on a wrong time" degrade in storage.
- **Artisan retention through regularisation:** the structural change is that artisans were historically paid seasonally and are now employed year-round — "Now, we have made them regular… Now young kids are coming into this business." This is the answer to the scaling constraint that would otherwise cap a handcraft business.
- **Formalisation as the barrier:** "we have come out from an unorganized world to an organized world. So, anybody who wants to compete with us has to get organized to our level." The company claims to be the first listed 100% Polki player.
- **Margin structure:** management argues luxury artwork jewellery cannot be priced on input build-up, which is why 29%+ EBITDA margins persist through gold volatility. Verifiable claim: peers' Polki-segment margins match, but their blended margin is diluted by low-margin gold.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin held at 29.04% in a soft Q4 and 29.48% for FY26. The stated mechanism is fixed-margin pricing on a design-led product where the customer is buying a trusted house and an artwork, not a metal weight — so gold price moves do not compress the spread the way they would for a generic jeweller. Management also expects the B2C shift to be margin-accretive ("you get a better margin… in B2C"), while immediately qualifying that it will not push pricing to the maximum because the piece is intended to hold asset value for the buyer: "we don't want to go very high with that because just want to give them a good asset value."
capex / expansion (watch slippage): The Jaipur flagship is the only dated commissioning item: ~30,000 sq ft, structure ready, interiors being accelerated, target of end-November 2026 ahead of the wedding season. Management explicitly refused to open at partial readiness — "I don't want to enter in a half level. I in a level where it is 75% or 80%. I want to finish it." Store-level capex, investment per store and payback were asked and not answered with numbers; management said each will be evaluated with partners on area capability. Design capacity is being added — seven to eight designers, more artisans, and a new master craftsman hired for the fusion collections.
capital allocation: Not discussed in any structured way — no dividend, buyback or debt commentary on the call. The stated philosophy is deliberate under-commitment: "being a Marwadi family, we have one thing that we should understand and then move things sensibly. Don't jump into it with a bulk and just doing all things together." Management explicitly declined to accept the franchise partner's pace, saying it will not "go jumping in that the franchise told us go for 10 more."
risks & watch-items:
- **Disclosure quality is the primary risk.** The CMD could not produce FY27 revenue or EBITDA targets on request, deflected repeatedly to "the website" and "the DRHP", and answered several quantitative questions ("what percentage of your sales would be gold", "what proportion from customer-led customisation") by disputing the premise rather than giving a number.
- Q4 revenue fell year on year while a shareholder noted listed peers grew 180–200%; the explanations offered (war-driven luxury caution Jan–Mar, December order pull-forward) are plausible but unquantified.
- Single-category, single-city concentration: 100% Polki, Jaipur-based artisan pool, one manufacturing facility.
- Franchise-led expansion transfers execution risk to a third party (Francorp) with a 30-store commitment the company itself is not underwriting.
- Exports are effectively zero (<1%) and the FY26 export was an unsolicited Instagram order — presented as a "gift to us", not a channel.
- Gold price inflation is pushing the company toward lighter-weight gold designs, which is why the gold-weight utilisation metric (31%) has fallen; the metric will keep looking weak regardless of business performance.
management quality / tone: Nitin Gilara is warm, discursive and clearly a product person rather than a finance person — the strongest passages are about craft (aesthetic blending of Jadau and temple jewellery, karigar working conditions, artisan families) and the weakest are about numbers. He was willing to push back on a shareholder framing rather than accept it ("why should I diversify my product portfolio? It is going so well"), which is candour, but the same instinct produced repeated non-answers on statistics. The inability to restate the company's own DRHP projections when asked twice is the single most concerning moment on the call for a company listed less than a year. Positively, he was direct about what has *not* started — exports, and store expansion beyond three.
non-obvious takeaways:
- The 31% capacity utilisation figure is a measurement artefact, not an operating problem — it tracks gold weight in a business where gold may be 30% of piece value and falling as designs get lighter. Anyone modelling off it will be wrong.
- The product-count drop from 21 to 10 is likewise recategorisation, not portfolio contraction — bridal sets and hand-wear were consolidated. Both metrics in the investor presentation mislead in the same direction.
- The real scaling constraint in handcraft jewellery is artisan supply, and management's answer is employment regularisation rather than automation — evidenced by a supplier family putting five daughters into inlay work.
- Management's own TAM arithmetic: ~70–80 lakh Indian weddings a year, of which ~80,000–1 lakh are HNI, each needing a bridal Polki set at an average ticket of ~INR 20 lakh — implying a ~INR 20,000 cr bridal Polki market in which Advit is ~1%.
- Diwali is explicitly *not* a season for luxury bridal jewellery — the season starts late November with NRI arrivals and the wedding calendar. That reframes which quarter to expect the flagship's contribution in.

group_structure.body:
- Rambhajo Buildcon Private Limited — Group Company
- Janak Nandini Buildwell Private Limited — Group Company
- M/s Rambhajo's — Promoter-associated jewellery entity (brand legacy)

segment_detail.title: Segment / subsidiary detail
segment_detail.body: Single-line business — 100% Jadau/Polki. Management rejects Titan and Kalyan as peers on the grounds that they are generic gold and diamond jewellers who "keep very little part of Jadau Polki. We are 100% Jadau Polki." The revenue split has moved toward B2C: "you can see it started touching 80 and 20." Gold content varies by piece rather than by rule — management gave the range explicitly: a new collection at ~30% gold value, men's buckles at ~70–80% gold value, and light earrings at very low gold content with Polki and coloured stone dominant. Exports were incidental in FY26 — an Instagram-originated US order where the customer absorbed a 50% tariff.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Manufacturing:** Gold Kundan Meena Polki Jadau jewellery (~95-98% of revenue), Cut setted Diamond jewellery with Polki (~1-3%)
- **Services:** Job work / other operating income

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- B2B - dealers, showrooms and jewellery retailers (82.41% of revenue in 9M FY26)
- B2C - exclusive made-to-order pieces (17.39% in 9M FY26)
- Job work (0.20% in 9M FY26)

cost_leadership.title: Supply chain integration (RHP report)
cost_leadership.body: Fully backward-integrated manufacturing under one roof (raw gold processing to finishing). Gold sourced from RBI-nominated banks and authorised vendors under gold-loan arrangements; diamond polki and precious/semi-precious stones from domestic open-market vendors on a spot basis (no long-term supply agreements). Raw materials are ~99.85% of cost of materials consumed (gold 76.44%, diamond polki 20.91%, stones 2.49% in 9M FY26).

order_book.title: Order book & pipeline
order_book.body: No order book disclosure. The business is seasonal and order-driven: management noted the September–December quarter is strong ("you will see an amazing increase in the sales") and that FY26 Q4 was partly cannibalised because orders received in December were completed and booked within that quarter. The next intake cycle was flagged for August, with artisans "all set to work hard." Post-IPO roadshows have produced an unexpected B2C funnel — management cited a Delhi roadshow attendee who subsequently bought five necklaces.

guidance.title: Guidance (CRITICAL — verify next quarter)
guidance.body:
- **Revenue growth / EBITDA:** **no numeric FY27 guidance given.** Asked directly for revenue and EBITDA targets, management deferred to figures already disclosed in the DRHP and to the five-year projections on the company website, and could not restate them on the call — "I will have to check that because that was a number which was calculated that time."
- **Store rollout:** franchise partner Francorp "has committed to us to bring up 30 stores in next three years." Company's own FY27 plan is deliberately smaller: "we are setting up at least around three stores in this year. The target is minimum three… others are bonus for this year."
- **Flagship commissioning:** the ~30,000 sq ft Jaipur store is targeted for operations "by say November end, when the NRIs start coming, the wedding season starts coming" — explicitly not by Diwali.
- **Margin:** no target, but management stated pricing is on fixed margins irrespective of product mix — "we are just keeping the fixed margins. Whatever the cost comes, we just keep the margins fixed on."
- **Exports:** no timeline or number. Middle East trade shows being planned; UK flagged as an opportunity after the 15 July free-trade opening.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body:
- **Retail/B2C rollout:** the core optionality. 30 franchise stores committed over three years, three self-driven stores in FY27, plus LOIs in progress on additional locations.
- **Men's jewellery:** cufflinks, belt buckles, brooches, kilangi and rings in Polki — a new category with higher gold content.
- **Gen-Z lightweight line:** everyday-wear pieces at fixed margins.
- **Cross-regional design fusion:** blending Rajasthani Jadau with South Indian temple jewellery to widen geographic appeal — a named product initiative for the coming collection.
- **Exports:** UK (post-FTA), Middle East shows, and the Indian diaspora. Management is candid that nothing is built yet — "we are not yet started on that part yet."

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Raw-material (gold/diamond polki) cost is 99.66-99.95% of total material cost - margins highly sensitive to gold prices; procured spot with no long-term contracts
- Predominantly wholesale (B2B) model with flexible credit terms to secure repeat orders - drives working-capital intensity
- Seasonality: higher volumes and margins during festive/wedding periods against largely fixed operating costs
- Gold procured from nominated banks/vendors under gold-loan arrangements (RBI framework)

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: EBITDA margin held at 29.04% in a soft Q4 and 29.48% for FY26. The stated mechanism is fixed-margin pricing on a design-led product where the customer is buying a trusted house and an artwork, not a metal weight — so gold price moves do not compress the spread the way they would for a generic jeweller. Management also expects the B2C shift to be margin-accretive ("you get a better margin… in B2C"), while immediately qualifying that it will not push pricing to the maximum because the piece is intended to hold asset value for the buyer: "we don't want to go very high with that because just want to give them a good asset value."

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Not discussed in any structured way — no dividend, buyback or debt commentary on the call. The stated philosophy is deliberate under-commitment: "being a Marwadi family, we have one thing that we should understand and then move things sensibly. Don't jump into it with a bulk and just doing all things together." Management explicitly declined to accept the franchise partner's pace, saying it will not "go jumping in that the franchise told us go for 10 more."

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The company is constructing a flagship retail store in Jaipur to grow its B2C business; manufacturing remains at the single leased 6,450 sq ft Jaipur unit (FY25 utilisation ~46%, leaving headroom).

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Nitin Gilara is warm, discursive and clearly a product person rather than a finance person — the strongest passages are about craft (aesthetic blending of Jadau and temple jewellery, karigar working conditions, artisan families) and the weakest are about numbers. He was willing to push back on a shareholder framing rather than accept it ("why should I diversify my product portfolio? It is going so well"), which is candour, but the same instinct produced repeated non-answers on statistics. The inability to restate the company's own DRHP projections when asked twice is the single most concerning moment on the call for a company listed less than a year. Positively, he was direct about what has *not* started — exports, and store expansion beyond three.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- 100+ year 'Rambhajo since 1921' brand heritage with promoter family of jewellers (26+ years experience)
- In-house, single-roof manufacturing enabling quality control, shorter lead times (25-30 days) and cost/security management
- Design innovation and customization in Kundan/Polki with unique non-repeated designs (catalogue kept private)
- Strong return ratios and profitability (FY25 RoE 55.79%, EBITDA margin 29.73%, PAT margin 20.30%)
- Volume growth of 38.92% in Fiscal 2025 vs Fiscal 2023 despite rising gold prices

risks.title: Risks & watch-items
risks.body:
- **Disclosure quality is the primary risk.** The CMD could not produce FY27 revenue or EBITDA targets on request, deflected repeatedly to "the website" and "the DRHP", and answered several quantitative questions ("what percentage of your sales would be gold", "what proportion from customer-led customisation") by disputing the premise rather than giving a number.
- Q4 revenue fell year on year while a shareholder noted listed peers grew 180–200%; the explanations offered (war-driven luxury caution Jan–Mar, December order pull-forward) are plausible but unquantified.
- Single-category, single-city concentration: 100% Polki, Jaipur-based artisan pool, one manufacturing facility.
- Franchise-led expansion transfers execution risk to a third party (Francorp) with a 30-store commitment the company itself is not underwriting.
- Exports are effectively zero (<1%) and the FY26 export was an unsolicited Instagram order — presented as a "gift to us", not a channel.
- Gold price inflation is pushing the company toward lighter-weight gold designs, which is why the gold-weight utilisation metric (31%) has fallen; the metric will keep looking weak regardless of business performance.

non_obvious.title: Non-obvious takeaways
non_obvious.body:
- The 31% capacity utilisation figure is a measurement artefact, not an operating problem — it tracks gold weight in a business where gold may be 30% of piece value and falling as designs get lighter. Anyone modelling off it will be wrong.
- The product-count drop from 21 to 10 is likewise recategorisation, not portfolio contraction — bridal sets and hand-wear were consolidated. Both metrics in the investor presentation mislead in the same direction.
- The real scaling constraint in handcraft jewellery is artisan supply, and management's answer is employment regularisation rather than automation — evidenced by a supplier family putting five daughters into inlay work.
- Management's own TAM arithmetic: ~70–80 lakh Indian weddings a year, of which ~80,000–1 lakh are HNI, each needing a bridal Polki set at an average ticket of ~INR 20 lakh — implying a ~INR 20,000 cr bridal Polki market in which Advit is ~1%.
- Diwali is explicitly *not* a season for luxury bridal jewellery — the season starts late November with NRI arrivals and the wedding calendar. That reframes which quarter to expect the flagship's contribution in.

commitments.title: Promises (RHP)
commitments.body:
- **Set up one flagship retail store in Jaipur to augment B2C sales (currently under construction).**
- **Repay/pre-pay certain outstanding borrowings from scheduled commercial banks using Rs 6,500 lakhs of Net Proceeds.**
- **Fund incremental working capital requirements using Rs 6,500 lakhs of Net Proceeds.**
- **Grow export sales (commenced to USA and Hong Kong in 9M FY26).**

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Augment B2C sales by setting up a flagship store in Jaipur (under construction)
- Expand customer relationships via new product lines, seasonal collections and personalized services
- Target new customer segments aligned with existing verticals
- Begin exports (USA and Hong Kong sales commenced in 9M FY26)

qoq_log.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)
qoq_log.body:
- **Q4 FY26 / FY26 (this):** FY26 total income INR 167.03 cr (+33.68%), EBITDA INR 49.24 cr at 29.48%, PAT INR 34.39 cr (+35.56%), diluted EPS INR 10.74. Q4 softer at INR 43.23 cr income, INR 12.56 cr EBITDA (29.04%), PAT INR 8.74 cr, EPS INR 2.79 — attributed to Jan–Mar war-driven luxury caution and December order pull-forward. Listed on NSE and BSE during the year. Active customers 96 → 274 across 21 states; exports initiated at <1% of revenue. Francorp franchise commitment of 30 stores over three years disclosed; minimum three stores targeted in FY27; ~30,000 sq ft Jaipur flagship targeted for end-November 2026. **No numeric FY27 revenue or EBITDA guidance given on the call.**
- _Q1 FY27 → check: did the Jaipur flagship stay on the end-November track; how many of the "minimum three" FY27 stores are actually signed (LOIs were said to be days away); whether Q1 revenue recovered the YoY decline seen in Q4; whether management provides a numeric FY27 target after being unable to restate DRHP projections; export progress against the UK/Middle East plans; whether the gold-weight utilisation metric is retained or replaced in the investor presentation._

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Entity / brand] Advit Jewels Limited is "Formerly Known as Advit Jewels Private Limited", trades as RAMBHAJO (BSE Scrip Code 544803), and its website/brand is www.rambhajo.com while its email domain is advitjewels.com - the promoters' operating heritage is attributed to "Rambhajo Jewellers".
- [Leadership] Board is promoter-family led: Mr. Nitin Gilara (Chairman & MD, 26 years in the jewellery segment, with Rambhajo Jewellers since 1999), Mr. Prateek Gilara (Whole Time Director, 18 years, with Rambhajo Jewellers since 2003), Mr. Vipul Gilara (Whole Time Director, 14+ years, re-designated Whole Time Director in 2025) and Mr. Krishna Gilara (Non-executive Director), alongside four Independent Directors.
- [Industry backdrop] Deck cites the Indian gems and jewellery retail market at "USD 80-85 billion in FY 2024" projected to "USD 140-155 billion by FY 2028", contributing "7% to the national GDP", employing "4.6 to 5 million people", accounting for "15% of India's merchandise exports" and "75% of the world's polished diamond exports", with the organized segment moving from a "36-38% market share in FY 2024 to 42-43% by FY 2028".
- [Gold price exposure] The deck's gold price series is 48,723.20 / 47,999.30 / 52,730.80 / 60,624.00 / 71,834.00 / 1,45,000.00 per 10 gram for FY21-FY26 - note the FY26 print of Rs 1,45,000.00 sits far outside the trend and outside the accompanying commentary, which stops at FY 2025 and speaks of an "almost 19% year-on-year increase".
- [Internal contradiction] Gold jewellery consumption of 430.50 tonnes is labelled two different ways: the text states "India's gold jewellery consumption stood at 430.5 tonnes in CY25", while the comparative chart carrying the same 430.50 figure is titled "Gold Jewellery Consumption In CY 2024" (India 430.50, Greater China 360.10, USA 126.80, Russia 39.50, Turkey 31.70). The bullet above that chart also names "The United States 126.8 tonnes, Russia 39.5 tonnes and Turkey 31.7 tonnes" without a year.
